source.title: DeepDecipher: Accessing and Investigating Neuron Activation in Large Language Models
source.authors: Albert Garde; Esben Kran; Fazl Barez

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports neuron-search case studies but does not test the claim's neuron-pole job shares. It also notes that highly activating examples may not represent a neuron's general behavior, a limitation relevant to V6.
record.gate_note: The case studies report token-search counts and semantic classifications from existing interpretability data, not proportions of neuron poles with one or more jobs or explanations evaluated on held-out activations. The discussion of highly activating examples is a stated limitation, not a result from a new evaluation.
record.test_reason: DeepDecipher is a tool paper that serves existing N2G, Neuroscope and Neuron Explainer data. Its case studies are token-search counts and informal semantic classifications in solu-6l-pile. It reports no share of neurons with one job, no cross-model shares, no InceptionV1 analysis, no attribution graphs and no held-out simulation scores. The remark that max-activating examples may not represent general behaviour is a cited limitation, not a result. It neither tests nor relies on the claim, so T6 fits better than the reader's T5.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors present DeepDecipher as an accessible API and interface to existing MLP-neuron interpretability data, adding no new methods. They note that its practical usability is broadly untested and that it inherits the max-activating-example limitations of the underlying methods.
record.recipe_differences: The paper presents an access and visualization tool for existing interpretability methods; it does not reproduce or evaluate the claim's audit method.

fits_no_version.finding: In solu-6l-pile, N2G token search returns different neuron counts across tokens (hola 0, hello 7; love 20, morose 0).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Token-search neuron counts vary by token and training-data language in small SoLU models.

fits_no_version.finding: Of 8 neurons responding to 'apple', 5 were judged about the company, 2 about the fruit, 1 ambiguous.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neurons responding to a homograph token mostly split by sense on inspection of N2G graphs.

record.peer_reviewed: XAI in Action: Past, Present, and Future Applications @ NeurIPS 2023
record.problems: No claim-specific quantitative evaluation is reported. The authors state that highly activating examples may not represent neurons' general behavior and that the tool's practical usability is broadly untested.

untested.parts: No neuron-pole job shares for Qwen3-32B or any model.
No interpretability shares across models, scale or MoE.
No InceptionV1 or canonical polysemantic neuron analysis.
No test of architecture, regularization or tools on the interpretable share.
No attribution graphs or circuit analysis.
Only states that max-activating examples may be unrepresentative; no test of explanation prediction failures.
Serves Bills et al. explanation scores but reports no distribution or new scoring.

record.verdict_notes: Tool paper. The appendix also gives search counts (the: 1976, he: 254, she: 126, dream: 4); these are API demonstrations, irrelevant to the claim, and need no rows.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not estimate the proportion of neuron poles with one or more jobs or the proportion not understood.
It does not compare interpretability shares across model sizes, dense and mixture-of-experts architectures, or models up to trillions of parameters.
It does not analyze InceptionV1's cat-and-car neuron or test recursive generalization against superposition.
It does not test the effects of architecture, regularization, tools, or model capacity on interpretability shares, and gives no InceptionV1-sized model estimates.
It does not build or evaluate attribution graphs or test whether neurons suffice as circuit units.
The paper cautions that highly activating examples may not represent general behavior, but does not test explanations against separate activating examples or measure prediction failures.
It does not score neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.
